title: Align a transcript and count the errors
brief: Align a hypothesis against a reference with a Levenshtein table, compute corpus word and character error rates, normalize transcripts, and test a gain with a paired bootstrap over utterances.
hints: Fill the edit table with E[i, 0] = i and E[0, j] = j first. Then E[i, j] is the minimum of a deletion, an insertion, and a diagonal step that costs 1 only when the words differ.
On the way back from E[n, m], test the diagonal move first, then the deletion, then the insertion. Call a diagonal move a hit when the two tokens are equal.
For corpus WER, keep two running totals, errors and reference words, and divide once at the end.
For CER, align list(ref) against list(hyp). Spaces are characters, so they count.
For normalize, replace punctuation with a space using re.sub(r"[^\w\s]", " ", text), not with nothing. Delete apostrophes first, split on whitespace, and look each word up in a dict of number words.

For paired_bootstrap, draw picks = rng.integers(0, n, size=(n_resamples, n)) once. Index errors_a, errors_b, and ref_lengths with the same picks, sum along axis 1, and divide the difference of summed errors by the summed lengths.
